textbookText: 17. Introduce angiogram and its importance.
Ans:- An angiogram is a medical imaging test that allows doctors to see the inside of blood vessels, including arteries and
veins, by injecting a special contrast dye into the bloodstream. This dye makes the vessels visible on X-rays, CT scans, or
MRI, helping to detect abnormalities such as blockages, narrowing, or aneurysms. It is a crucial tool for diagnosing vascular
conditions and planning appropriate medical or surgical treatments.
Importance of Angiogram:
1. Detects blockages or narrowing in arteries that may lead to heart attacks or strokes.
2. Identifies aneurysms or weak spots in blood vessel walls.
3. Guides medical procedures like angioplasty, stent placement, or bypass surgery.
4. Monitors blood flow to organs and tissues.
5. Enables early detection of vascular diseases, reducing the risk of severe complications.

19. Study the concept map given below and answer the following questions.
i) What type of blood circulation is shown in the concept map?
Ans:-Systemic blood circulation is shown in the concept map.
ii) In which parts of the concept map do arteries and veins play a role in blood circulation?
Ans:- Arteries carry blood from the left ventricle to the kidney. And veins carry blood from the kidney to the right auricle of
the heart.
iii) In which parts of the concept map pure and impure blood flow?
Ans:- Pure (oxygenated) blood flows from the left ventricle to the kidney. And impure (deoxygenated) blood flows from the
kidney to the right auricle.
